Two Anthropic engineers will teach you more about building AI Agents in 16 minutes than most paid courses ever will

Barry Zhang and Mahesh Murag built Claude Skills at Anthropic
In this talk, they lay out the full architecture and the thinking behind it

📌 The core insight is simple :

Today's AI agents are like a genius with no work experience
They can reason, write code, call APIs
But they don't know YOUR processes, YOUR tools, YOUR domain

Intelligence ≠ expertise

So Anthropic stopped building separate agents for every use case
They built one general agent + a skill system instead

A skill is literally a folder
Markdown instructions. Scripts. Assets. That's it

📌 Here's what they cover:

→ Why code is the universal interface for agents, not custom scaffolding
→ How skills are progressively loaded to protect the context window
→ The split between MCP (access to external tools) and Skills (expertise)
→ How Fortune 100 companies are encoding internal workflows as Skills
→ Why non-technical teams in finance, legal, and recruiting are building skills too

The architecture they're converging on :

Agent loop + Runtime + MCP servers for connectivity + Skills for expertise

Deploying Claude to a new domain = the right MCP servers + the right skill library

They already used this to launch Claude for financial services and life sciences

Day 1&2 at VivaTech 2026. I'm still processing it...

I walked into Hall 7 yesterday's morning not really knowing what to expect

By noon my feet hurt, my phone was at 30%, and my notebook was full

Here's the thing nobody prepares you for: the scale. The travelator just keeps going. The ceilings are impossibly high!
You turn a corner expecting one more booth and there's an entire second world behind it

But that's not what I'll remember...

What I'll remember is the conversations  

The founder who explained his entire product to me in 90 seconds because he only had 90 seconds

The engineer demoing something he'd clearly been up until 3am fixing

The stranger in the coffee line who turned out to be building the exact thing I'd been thinking about for months

This is the part of tech that doesn't fit in a screenshot
The energy of thousands of people who actually build things in the same room, all slightly sleep-deprived, all a little obsessed

I came here thinking I'd be observing. Instead I spent the whole day talking.

Two more days to go and I already don't want it to end !

If you're here too, come say hi. I'm the one with the dying phone and the full notebook👋

#VivatechAmbassador
